transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-03
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Riley Park (Redwood) — Alex Gomez, Priya Rao, Samir Patel (CalderaTech)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be short): Discussed cost spikes on inference during batch uploads and steady-state latency SLOs; Redwood suggested dedicated pool pilot and offered observability/workbook.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I see Alex, Priya, Samir — thanks for taking the time. Quick agenda: health/costs, recent latency incidents, options (hosted vs dedicated), pilot proposal, security checklist.

[01:02] Alex Gomez: Yeah thanks Maya. I'll be honest, we've been seeing token costs spike in May. Some of that is seasonal traffic, some maybe prompt bloat. Priya, do you want to add infra context?

[01:18] Priya Rao: Sure. We have a mix of medium and long-form generation calls. Peak windows are around 11am PST and 8pm PST. We batch some requests client-side but not consistently. Also we saw a few 5xx errors last week when our upstream retries spiked.

[02:03] Riley Park: Got it. When you say token costs spiked, any rough numbers—percent increase month-over-month?

[02:12] Alex Gomez: About 42% MoM for the last month. Mainly per-token charges but also more re-runs because of prompt quality. There's also a hit from higher temperature stochastic runs on some features.

[03:00] Maya Chen: Ok that's helpful. Two angles we usually look at: reduce unit cost (batching, quantization, model variant) and reduce error/redo rate (prompt hygiene, retries, idempotency). For the cost piece, Dedicated pool can give you predictable throughput and a lower per-token unit cost if you commit.

[04:05] Samir Patel: Quick question—what's the fallback story if dedicated saturates? We can't have degraded user UX.

[04:20] Riley Park: Good callout. We recommend a smart routing policy: primary to Dedicated, fallback to hosted or a smaller variant model. It can be region/latency based. We also have automatic TTL for cached prefixes to reduce load.

[05:00] Alex Gomez: About the latency spikes, last week's incident telemetry showed tail latency increasing to 1.2s at p95 for long sequences; p99 was spiking to 2.7s during one window. We need steady-state p95 under 800ms.

[05:34] Priya Rao: The sequences in question were across batches with many past-key-values (KV cache) warm-ups. We suspect KV cache eviction/imbalanced routing during autoscaling caused re-compute.

[06:10] Riley Park: That aligns with what we've seen in other customers. Two knobs: ensure model variant with KV-efficient kernels and tune autoscaling thresholds (ramp slower, pre-warm instances for predicted windows). Also batching strategies matter — smaller micro-batches during tail windows can help.

[07:08] Alex Gomez: Can you quantify cost savings if we switch to Dedicated? We need concrete numbers for our finance team.

[07:22] Maya Chen: Yes — we'll share a tailored pricing sheet. Ballpark: customers with stable peak windows and predictable throughput saw 20–35% lower per-token costs on Dedicated, sometimes more when paired with quantized variants. We'll run a model for your traffic profile.

[08:05] Samir Patel: Security is also a blocker for us. We need SOC 2, SSO/SAML, KMS integration. Where do you stand on those?

[08:22] Maya Chen: Redwood has SOC 2 Type II, SSO/SAML and KMS integrations for Private deployments. For Dedicated we can provide audit logs, RBAC, and optional VPC peering. We'll attach the security artifacts.

[09:10] Priya Rao: Do you support customer-managed keys (HSM)? We need to ensure raw data isn't accessible to the control plane.

[09:27] Riley Park: For Private deployments yes. For Dedicated there's an option to bring-your-own-key via KMS integrations; we can surface more details in the security FAQ I'll link.

[10:12] Alex Gomez: Okay good. On timeline — we'd like a pilot to validate cost and latency within the next 6 weeks. What does the pilot typically include?

[10:30] Maya Chen: Typical pilot is 4–6 weeks: ingest a representative traffic sample, run A/B between hosted and Dedicated, measure tail latency and token cost, and test routing/fallback. We recommend a small committed pool for the pilot so scheduling is predictable.

[11:15] Priya Rao: Are there any caveats around data residency for the pilot? We need EU-only for some data.

[11:29] Riley Park: Yes, you can pin region; Dedicated pools can be region-scoped. We'll document region availability and ensure the control plane behaves as your compliance requires.

[12:10] Alex Gomez: Could you also run a quick modelling exercise during the pilot? I want to see sensitivity to prompt length and batch size.

[12:28] Maya Chen: Absolutely. We'll provide a cost workbook and run a sensitivity analysis. If you can share an anonymized traffic snapshot, Riley can run the perf tests.

[13:40] Samir Patel: One risk we need to call out—if we commit and then traffic drops, how hard is it to resize or exit?

[13:55] Maya Chen: We structure commitments with a baseline and then allow change windows. For the pilot we recommend a small baseline so you're not locked in; then scale if results are positive. We can go through contract language with legal.

[15:02] Priya Rao: A few quick technical clarifications: what quantization levels do you recommend for our T5-like model? And how does that affect latency?

[15:20] Riley Park: For models similar to T5 we usually start with 8-bit symmetric quantization for generation workloads; it's a good balance. In our testing, next-token latency often stays within 5–15% of FP16, but throughput/cost improves. We'll test with your model and give exact numbers.

[16:10] Alex Gomez: On observability, we need per-route cost breakdown and token-level attribution. Can Redwood provide that?

[16:23] Maya Chen: Yes, Redwood Console has token-level breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and traces. We can configure dashboards for your key endpoints and share a demo link.

[17:05] Speaker 2: (background noise) ...sorry — I didn't catch the last bit about traces, could you repeat?

[17:13] Maya Chen: Sure — Console supports trace hooks and you can link your APM. We'll show a short demo in the follow-up.

[18:00] Alex Gomez: If we run A/B and Dedicated wins on latency but not cost, do you offer hybrid routing by route?

[18:15] Riley Park: Yes — route-level policies let you send latency-critical routes to Dedicated and cheaper routes to hosted. That's an often-used pattern.

[19:20] Priya Rao: What's the typical lead time to provision a Dedicated pool for a pilot?

[19:32] Maya Chen: For our standard regions it's usually 3–7 business days once contracts are signed. For VPC/private or on-prem it can take longer.

[20:10] Samir Patel: Anything we should be careful about in the pilot design?

[20:22] Riley Park: Make sure your sample covers peak windows and includes the longer-context prompts, because those are where caching and KV behavior show up. Also include error cases so we can measure re-run rates.

[21:05] Alex Gomez: Great. Let's recap next steps. Maya?

[21:12] Maya Chen: Recap: we'll send a tailored pricing sheet and cost workbook by Monday (2027-06-07). Riley will request the anonymized traffic snapshot and run an initial 100-query perf test, results by 2027-06-09. We'll attach SOC2 and security artifacts. Caldera to confirm pilot KPIs by 2027-06-10. We'll also schedule the 1-hour perf bench during week of 6/14.

[22:08] Priya Rao: Sounds good. One more question — any known outages or recent incidents in April/May we should be aware of?

[22:20] Riley Park: No major platform outages affecting Dedicated, some minor routing incidents in April that were fixed; we'll include a short incident digest.

[23:00] Alex Gomez: Thanks — that's helpful.

[23:10] Maya Chen: Ok wrapping up — we'll follow up with the docs and pricing. If anything else comes up ping me. Thanks everyone.

[23:40] Meeting end.
